title: ResponseEntity and HTTP status codes
summary: Return explicit status codes, headers and DTO bodies for successful and failed requests.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: ResponseEntity in Spring Boot in Hindi | Handling HttpStatus while creating REST API

richText: ResponseEntity<T> carries a status code, headers and an optional body of type T. A controller can choose them explicitly instead of returning only a body.
200 OK fits a successful read or an update that returns data. 201 Created fits a newly created resource; a Location header tells the client where it can be read.
204 No Content means success with no response body. Do not return a JSON body with 204.
400 Bad Request describes invalid client input. 401 means authentication is required or failed. 403 means the authenticated caller is not allowed.
404 Not Found fits a resource that cannot be found or exposed to the caller. 409 Conflict fits a request that conflicts with current resource state.
Choose status codes from the result of the operation. The annotation @PostMapping does not make every response 201 automatically.
These methods belong in a controller mapped to /journal. JournalResponse is an application DTO, and the service must apply the current user’s ownership rules.
findVisible returns Optional<JournalResponse>. No visible result produces 404; a saved result produces 200 with a body.
create returns 201, the saved DTO and a Location such as /journal/42. The example assumes the service returns an identifier safe for a path segment.
Use request DTOs to limit which fields clients can supply. Do not allow a request body to set internal IDs, roles or ownership unchecked.
ResponseEntity controls the response envelope. @RestController and message converters still handle converting the DTO to JSON.
Keep common error shapes in exception advice. Handle authentication failures through Spring Security’s entry point or access-denied handler when they occur before the controller.
Returning 200 with a body saying “error” makes client behavior harder to interpret. Match the HTTP status to the actual result.
